title: Prefill Solidarity Admission and Attention Latency Fence
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a two-part runtime enhancement to reduce tail latency for mixed-length workloads: (1) a "solidarity admission" heuristic that groups very short prefill requests into small dedicated micro-batches when higher-throughput batches would otherwise delay them, and (2) an "attention latency fence" that reserves a bounded fast-path budget on each GPU for attention-heavy decode bursts. Goal is to reduce p99 prefill latency and p99 end-to-end decode latency without regressing throughput or cost per token for steady-state workloads.
acceptance_criteria: p99 prefill latency reduced by >=25% for mixed short+long workload traces gathered from production in feb-2026
No more than 5% regression in aggregate token/sec on our standard Llama-variant benchmark cluster in non-burst scenarios
Automated integration tests exercising solidarity admission edge cases (single-request micro-batch, starvation recovery) implemented and passing in CI
Monitoring dashboards show stable fast-path budget usage and no sustained starvation events after 24h of canary traffic
implementation_notes: Solidarity admission: add admission discriminator that identifies 'micro-prefill' candidates (prefill length < 16 tokens OR predicted decode < 20 tokens) and routes them to a micro-batch queue with max size 8 and low-wait timer (4ms). When micro-batch queue is below threshold it is allowed to dispatch immediately on the fast kernel path optimized for short sequence lengths.

Attention latency fence: maintain a per-GPU circular budget of N attention-optimized slots (configurable, default 6) that cannot be consumed by bulk batches. When budget is full, attention-heavy requests are allowed but routed to a fallback attention kernel that is slower but fairer; budget replenishes on completion or after timeout. This prevents long attention bursts from monopolizing the fast-path kernels.

Kernel selection: extend kernel planner to expose 'fast-path-friendly' tags for fused attention kernels and prefetched KV layouts; the planner will prefer these tags for micro-batches while ensuring compatibility with model quantization profiles.

Backpressure & fallback: micro-batch admission emits soft metrics and can fall back to normal admission if steady-state throughput drops below configured threshold for >10s. Fallback path uses existing batching behavior to preserve throughput.

Config: expose solidarity admission and fence parameters in runtime config and console UI for canary customers and internal experiments; defaults disabled for private deployments unless explicitly enabled.
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission discriminator logic and micro-batch timer semantics
Load tests using mixed-length replay trace (trace id: replay-2026-02-mixed-3) to validate p50/p95/p99 improvements
Kernel smoke test on quantized and non-quantized model builds to confirm fast-path selection correctness
Canary rollout to 10 dedicated capacity nodes for 48h, compare against control group with telemetry: p99 prefill, p99 decode, tokens/sec, GPU utilization
Chaos test: simulate a sudden traffic spike of short requests and verify budget enforcement prevents fast-path saturation
rollout_plan: Feature branch + review: implement on branch runtime/admission/solidarity; internal design doc linked
PRs: runtime, kernel-planner, and metrics instrumentations must land together and be feature-flagged
Canary: enable feature-flag on 10 nodes (dedicated) and run the mixed-length workload replay for 48h
Gradual ramp: if canary metrics meet acceptance criteria, enable on 25% of serving fleets for 72h, then 75% for 24h, then globally subject to infra approvals
Rollback triggers: sustained tokens/sec drop >5% for 30m, or p99 regressions >10% for 30m
metrics_and_dashboards: New metrics: solidarity.micro_batch_size.hist, solidarity.wait_time.ms.pXX, fence.fast_path_slots_in_use, fence.replenish_rate
Dashboards: build 'Solidarity Admission' dashboard in Console showing p50/p95/p99 prefill latency by request-length bucket, micro-batch occupancy, and fast-path slot saturation
Alert rules: alert if fence.fast_path_slots_in_use > 90% for >5m or solidarity.wait_time.ms.p99 > 20ms for >10m
Benchmark comparisons: generate before/after token/sec curves and normalized cost-per-token for the Llama-variant benchmark used in ENG perf suite
